the regulation of signaling networks in the cell.
the control of cell differentiation by signaling pathways.
the mechanisms by which cells control the activity of signal transduction pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MPT5 PUF-family RNA binding protein controls signaling in a MAP- kinase pathway by repressing the protein levels of pathway components and by inhibiting the kinase activity of a MAP kinase.
Mpt5 is a novel regulator of the MAP-kinase signaling pathway that represses signaling output in the absence of extracellular stimuli.
this work shows how a protein that binds to the untranslated regions of specific mRNA species controls the activity of the MAP-kinase cascade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Puf RNA-binding protein represses the MAP-kinase signaling pathway by binding to the mRNAs encoding two pathway components, and thereby controls the output of the signaling pathway.

Mpt5, a PUF-family protein, regulates a signaling cascade in the yeast filamentous pathway by controlling the stability of the pathway components, Ste7 and Tec1, and the activity of the MAP-kinase Kss1.
MPT5 represses Ste7 and Tec1 mRNA levels, and thereby controls KSS1 activity and the output of the MAP-kinase signaling pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of the MAPK pathway by the RNA binding protein Mpt5 is a mechanism that prevents inappropriate signaling.
the MAP-kinase signaling cascade is controlled by an RNA-binding protein, which represses the expression of pathway components.
RNA-binding proteins can regulate signaling pathways by controlling the expression of pathway components, as well as by controlling the translation of signaling proteins.
